subject: 2025 Disability Fair Planning and City Accessibility
overview: The commission reviewed recent physical accessibility upgrades at City Hall and scheduled the 2025 Disability Fair for late April. The body also discussed transit advocacy, building renovation goals, and public safety programs for residents with disabilities.

items.title: Introductions and Guest Welcome
items.summary: The commission introduced its members and welcomed resident John Shea, who shared his experiences with vision loss and mobility challenges.

items.title: Commission Mandate and Program Review
items.summary: Director Frances Nwajei outlined the commission's ordinance-based role in advocating for residents and highlighted recent work, including large-print form assistance and Community Access Monitoring training.

items.title: Physical Equipment and Assistive Technology Upgrades
items.summary: The commission reported the arrival of 12 new chairs with arms for the chambers and the procurement of updated assistive listening receivers using ARPA funding.

items.title: Commuter Rail and Transit Advocacy
items.summary: Members discussed ongoing advocacy for accessibility improvements at the West Medford commuter rail station and noted the MBTA's renewed focus on community engagement and wayfinding signage.

items.title: Public Space and Playground Consultation
items.summary: The body reviewed its history of consulting on accessible design for local playgrounds, including Carr Park and the McGlynn school play space.

items.title: Building Infrastructure and Facility Goals
items.summary: Director Nwajei discussed long-term goals for public bathroom accessibility renovations and reported on recent lighting fixture upgrades within City Hall.

items.title: City Hall Elevator and Emergency Testing
items.summary: The commission reported that the City Hall elevator underwent extensive wiring repairs and successfully passed emergency communication testing during a recent fire alarm.

items.title: 2025 Disability Fair Scheduling
items.summary: The commission scheduled the next Disability Fair for April 26, 2025, from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., with a rain date of April 27.

items.title: Community Complaint Trends and Code Enforcement
items.summary: Members reviewed common complaints regarding accessible parking violations, sidewalk obstructions, and the legal requirements for snow and ice removal.

items.title: Service Animals and SMART 911 Programs
items.summary: The commission discussed service animal regulations and planned to invite Captain Clemente to a future meeting to discuss the SMART 911 emergency registration system.
